newsitem.title: UK: UK stocks outlook - FTSE braced for July 2 Budget.
newsitem.headline: UK stocks outlook - FTSE braced for July 2 Budget.

text.p: UK stocks are likely to remain subdued and edgy until the middle of next week as investors await crucial economic policy decisions on both sides of the Atlantic.

"People are not going to commit new funds to the market before the UK Budget and the FOMC meeting in the U.S," said Jeremy Batstone, head of research at NatWest Stockbrokers. "The week will begin very quietly and then all hell will be let loose."
Fears that the new UK government's first budget on Wednesday could target taxes at corporates rather than the consumer sector have already knocked UK blue-chips off their record peaks.
The FTSE 100 index was already standing some 200-points below its all-time high of 4,796 set two weeks ago. By 1300 GMT on Friday the FTSE was down 33.4 points at 4,624.5.

Much of the recent damage was done by reports that Chancellor of the Exchequer (finance minister) Gordon Brown was planning to cut or abolish Advance Corporation Tax, (ACT) which allows pension funds to claim back tax on dividend payouts.
